assumedUseCase: Retrieve site traffic metrics, pageviews, and visitor stats to generate automated analytics reports or summaries.
tldr: Plausible Analytics does not offer OAuth 2.0 for third-party integrations, authenticating API access exclusively via Personal Access Tokens. Users must manually create an API key in their Plausible account settings and provide it to your application.

classification.rationale: Plausible Analytics does not support standard OAuth 2.0 authorization flows for third-party applications. API authentication relies on static Personal Access Tokens passed as HTTP Bearer tokens.

flags.detail: Stats API access requires an active Business plan or higher subscription.

evidence.note: Plausible documentation notes Stats API access is available on Business plans or higher.

flags.detail: API tokens do not support automated refresh flows. If a key is deleted or revoked by the user, API requests fail until a new key is provided.

evidence.note: API access relies entirely on user-generated static Personal Access Tokens.

firstToken.conditions: Developer or user creates a Personal Access Token in Plausible team settings.

evidence.note: API key generation takes seconds inside the Plausible web app.

production.conditions: Application backend securely prompts for, validates, and stores end-user Plausible API keys.

evidence.note: No app submission or review process exists; production delivery depends solely on app client implementation.

prerequisites.detail: Access to the Stats API requires a paid Business plan or higher tier.
The user creating the API key must have an Owner, Admin, Editor, or Billing role on the target Plausible team.

steps.title: Verify plan eligibility and site ID
steps.detail: Confirm that your Plausible account is on a Business plan or higher and obtain the domain name (site_id) configured in Plausible.
steps.agentHelp: Document the site_id format and subscription prerequisite in UI microcopy.

steps.title: Generate Personal Access Token
steps.detail: Log in to Plausible, navigate to account settings -> API Keys, click New API Key, select Stats API or Sites API, and save the token.
steps.agentHelp: Provide direct step-by-step UI copy for users creating an API key inside Plausible.

steps.title: Configure HTTP Authorization header
steps.detail: Store the token securely and send it with every request as an Authorization header ('Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>').
steps.agentHelp: Write HTTP client wrapper code that appends the Bearer token header to all Plausible API calls.

steps.title: Execute test query against Stats API
steps.detail: Make a GET request to the aggregate endpoint with the site_id parameter to verify authentication and data retrieval.
steps.agentHelp: Generate script to execute test API calls and parse site metric response payloads.

steps.title: Implement rate limit and error handling
steps.detail: Handle 600 request/hour rate limits and 401 unauthorized errors gracefully in case the key is invalid or revoked.
steps.agentHelp: Implement retry handling, backoff timers, and UI alerts prompting users to update their API key if invalidated.

gotchas.title: No Public OAuth 2.0 Flow
gotchas.detail: Plausible does not provide an OAuth flow for seamless end-user authorization. Users must manually paste API keys into your application.
gotchas.mitigation: Design your application onboarding to collect and validate user API keys manually.

gotchas.title: Paid Subscription Required for Stats API
gotchas.detail: Stats API access is restricted to accounts on a Business plan or higher.
gotchas.mitigation: Warn users in your setup interface that a paid Plausible Business plan is necessary.

gotchas.title: Hourly Rate Limit
gotchas.detail: API requests are capped at 600 requests per hour by default.
gotchas.mitigation: Cache results where possible or request elevated limits from Plausible for Enterprise users.

gotchas.title: Viewer and Guest Role Restrictions
gotchas.detail: Team members with Viewer or Guest roles cannot generate API keys in Plausible.
gotchas.mitigation: Inform users that an account with Owner, Admin, Editor, or Billing permissions is required to generate keys.

uncertainties.why: Official documentation makes no mention of third-party OAuth 2.0 support or partner integration portals.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Contact Plausible support (https://plausible.io/contact) or monitor developer documentation updates.
